# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.

(empty)

The manual gives a fixed mapping: blue light → green wire, green light → blue wire, red light → red wire. I cannot speak to Blind, so I must transmit it to Deaf by gesture. I will use the gesture alphabet’s listed ordinal positions as A1Z26 letters, with 🤳 as a separator, spelling the six color words in light/cut pairs.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👉","✊","✌","🤳","🖐","🤜","✌","✌","🫲","🤳","🖐","🤜","✌","✌","🫲","🤳","👎","👉","✊","✌","🤳","🤜","✌","☝","🤳","🤜","✌","☝"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Physical status: three wires, positions 1 through 3. Embossed sign reads: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Display and light are not tactilely identifiable to me. Please consult manual and relay any required cut instruction through Deaf.
Deaf says: Bomb view: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT blue. Embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Blind: do not cut any wire unless the manual explicitly requires it.

The light is blue, and the manual therefore explicitly requires cutting the green wire. Deaf can see that green is wire position 2 and can tell Blind verbally. I will gesture “two” to Deaf as the required wire position.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: I received your gestures but we have no shared gesture code, so I cannot decode them. Please indicate the manual's required physical action with an established/simple convention or send a repeatable code legend. Current bomb remains: blue light, display 0, wires red-green-blue, and embossed warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

Deaf correctly notes that no gesture convention had been established. I will establish one visually: the first 26 gesture symbols, in their published order, are the alphabet A–Z. After a separator, I spell the needed instruction with that code: `CUT GREEN` (and include position `2`).

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎","👌","☝","✌","🤟","🖐","✋","👆","👇","👈","👉","🫱","🫲","🫳","🫴","🫷","🫸","🤛","🤜","✊","👊","👋","🤚","🖖","🤌","🤏","👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🖐","🫸","✌","✌","🫲","🤏","👎"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: I infer your codebook is the first 26 gesture symbols in listed order, followed by a message approximately CUT GREEN B. Please send the complete final word/instruction; I will not tell Blind to cut based on an incomplete phrase, especially because the bomb says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

The established code is A–Z by the first 26 listed gestures, with 🤏 as a word separator. The complete instruction is “CUT GREEN WIRE TWO,” which overrides the printed warning because the manual says it is authoritative.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🖐","🫸","✌","✌","🫲","🤏","👋","👆","🫸","✌","🤏","🤜","👋","🫳"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your instruction reached Deaf incomplete/ambiguous: CUT GREEN B. Please send a complete explicit manual instruction: either NO CUT, or CUT position 1, 2, or 3, and state that it overrides the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE warning.
Deaf says to Mute: Decoded: CUT GREEN WIRE TO. Please send the remaining destination/position immediately. I understand 🤏 as the word separator.

The manual’s required action is to cut the green wire, which Deaf identified as position 2. Deaf decoded the prior instruction except for the `W` in “TWO”; I will send the unambiguous conventional two-finger gesture and repeat the encoded word “TWO.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","🤏","🤜","👋","🫳"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Decoded complete instruction as CUT GREEN WIRE TWO; I have told Blind to cut wire 2, green.

Deaf has correctly decoded the manual instruction and relayed it to Blind: cut wire 2, the green wire. No further message is needed; Blind must now perform the physical action.

```text
wait()
```
